questions.prompt: Explain, using ideas about acceleration, why speed limits near schools are usually low.
questions.modelAnswer: A vehicle can only decelerate at a limited rate (its brakes and tyres limit the acceleration). At a higher speed it takes longer, and much further, to reduce the velocity to zero, so it can't stop in time if a child steps out. Keeping speeds low means the car can stop in a shorter distance, reducing the chance and severity of accidents.
rubric: Higher speed needs more time and distance to stop
